g1|variants|consignment.summary: Customer consignment processes allow companies to store goods at a customer location while retaining ownership until the customer consumes or sells them. Variants differ by the business phase (Pick-up, Issue, Return, Fill-up) and whether billing or inventory movement is immediately triggered.

variants.name: Consignment Fill-up
variants.when_used: Delivering stock to customer location for consignment storage without transferring ownership.
variants.key_config: Sales document type KB uses item category KBN with special stock indicator W, triggering movement 631 for consignment fill-up.

variants.name: Consignment Issue
variants.when_used: Customer consumes stock from consignment inventory, triggering ownership transfer and billing.
variants.key_config: Sales document type KE uses item category KEN with special stock indicator W, issuing stock via movement 633 and billing the customer.

variants.name: Consignment Pickup
variants.when_used: Retrieving unsold consignment inventory from the customer location back to our plant.
variants.key_config: Sales document type KA uses item category KAN with special stock indicator W, bringing physical stock back via movement 634.

variants.name: Consignment Returns
variants.when_used: Customer returns previously issued consignment stock that they had already consumed and billed.
variants.key_config: Sales document type KR uses item category KRN, returning stock to consignment inventory via movement 632 with credit memo.

g1|core|consignment|consignment fill-up.title: Consignment Fill-up (Order-to-Cash)
g1|core|consignment|consignment fill-up.story: Imagine you send boxes of toys to a store to keep on their shelves, but you still own the toys until they sell them. This process moves stock from your warehouse to the customer's consignment stock location without billing them yet, using sales document type KB.
g1|core|consignment|consignment fill-up.why_business_needs_it: It allows a company to place inventory closer to the customer to speed up sales, ensuring the customer only pays when the goods are actually used or sold, while maintaining accurate stock ownership in SAP S/4HANA.

modules.role: Creates the consignment fill-up order (KB), triggers the outbound delivery, and hands off shipping requirements to inventory management without generating a billing document.
modules.hands_off_to: MM-IM (Inventory Management) for goods issue posting (movement type 631) to move stock into special customer consignment stock.

modules.role: Processes the physical movement of goods out of company-owned stock into customer consignment stock based on the outbound delivery.
modules.hands_off_to: FI (Financial Accounting) for updating stock values if configured, though fill-ups are typically non-valuated in standard special stock setups.

g1|core|consignment|consignment issue.title: Consignment Issue
g1|core|consignment|consignment issue.story: Think of keeping toys at a friend's house where you only pay for the ones you actually play with at the end of the day. In SAP Order-to-Cash, Consignment Issue (KE) allows a company to issue stock from consignment inventory to a customer, transferring ownership and creating a customer invoice only upon consumption.
g1|core|consignment|consignment issue.why_business_needs_it: This process allows companies to maintain stock at the customer location without immediate revenue recognition, improving customer service while retaining ownership until actual usage occurs. It ensures timely billing and accurate inventory reduction based on actual customer consumption.

modules.role: Receives the consignment issue order KE, processes the delivery with movement type 633, and generates the billing document based on delivery quantity.
modules.hands_off_to: MM (Materials Management) for stock posting and FI (Financial Accounting) for revenue posting.

modules.role: Manages consignment stock special stock indicators and executes goods movement type 633 to post goods issue from customer consignment stock.
modules.hands_off_to: FI (Financial Accounting) for inventory valuation updates.

modules.role: Posts revenue, cost of goods sold, and customer receivables when the consignment issue billing document is created.

g1|core|consignment|consignment pickup.title: Consignment Pickup
g1|core|consignment|consignment pickup.story: Consignment Pickup is the process where a customer returns unsold consignment stock back to our warehouse, and we receive it back onto our books without immediately owing them money. Technically, the sales department creates an order type KA with item category KAN, which triggers an outbound delivery with movement type 634 to move the physical stock from customer consignment special stock back to company-owned plant stock.
g1|core|consignment|consignment pickup.why_business_needs_it: This business process allows companies to retrieve unsold goods from a customer location when the consignment agreement ends or inventory needs rotation, ensuring accurate inventory valuation and physical stock reconciliation without generating a financial credit memo. Without it, customer consignment inventory remains indefinitely parked at customer sites, leading to inaccurate stock reporting and potential inventory shrinkage.

g1|core|consignment|consignment returns.title: Consignment Returns
g1|core|consignment|consignment returns.story: When a customer sends back unsold consignment goods that they previously stored at their location, the system records the physical return and restores it to stock without issuing an immediate credit until the return is formally inspected and billed. Technically, Consignment Returns (KR) process customer-owned stock back into company-managed consignment inventory through a dedicated sales document type KR, sales item category KRN, schedule line category DN, and movement type 632, ultimately triggering billing relevance G for credit settlement.
g1|core|consignment|consignment returns.why_business_needs_it: This process ensures accurate accounting and inventory tracking when customers return goods they never actually purchased. It enables precise control over customer consignment stock balances and protects financial reporting by separating physical returns from billing until final inspection.

g1|panel|consignment.otc_impact: Consignment processes in Order-to-Cash manage customer-held inventory owned by our company until it is consumed or returned, spanning Fill-up, Issue, Pickup, and Returns. It modifies standard OTC flows by deferring revenue recognition and billing until the customer reports consumption via Consignment Issue, while maintaining non-valuated special stock in Extended Warehouse Management (EWM) and Inventory Management (IM). When integrated with OTC, it prevents premature billing, ensures accurate stock visibility across customer locations, and directly impacts DSO (Days Sales Outstanding) and carrying costs.

panel_qa.question: How do we handle inventory ownership and valuation shifts from consignment fill-up to issue without triggering premature revenue recognition?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Consignment fill-up uses sales document type KB with item category KBN, which creates a non-billing outbound delivery and updates special stock 'W' (customer consignment) in Inventory Management without hitting FI. Revenue recognition is deferred because item category KBN has the billing relevance flag set to blank in table T184. When the customer actually consumes the material, we process a Consignment Issue using sales document type KE and item category KEN. Item category KEN is configured with billing relevance 'A' (delivery-related billing) and a pricing procedure that calculates revenue upon goods issue. This ensures accounting recognizes revenue and cost of goods sold only at the point of customer consumption.
panel_qa.trap: We just bill the customer right when the delivery trucks leave our warehouse for the fill-up order.

panel_qa.question: What is the end-to-end integration architecture between Sales Order Management, EWM, and Finance for consignment issue processing in S/4HANA?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: The end-to-end flow begins in SD with sales document type KE (Consignment Issue) triggering an outbound delivery document in LE-SHP or Decentralized EWM via qRFC. EWM creates a warehouse request and outbound delivery order, posting a goods issue with movement type 631 for special stock indicator 'W'. This goods issue posts a financial entry moving the inventory from company-owned consignment stock to cost of goods sold (or unbilled receivables depending on setup), while reducing physical stock at the customer location. Finally, billing document type F2 references the delivery using copy control routine 051 at item level, generating the AR invoice. This guarantees seamless transactional hand-offs across logistics and finance modules.
panel_qa.trap: Consignment issues bypass warehouse management entirely and update financial statements directly from the sales order entry.

panel_qa.question: Why use specific order and item categories for consignment variants instead of reusing standard sales orders with special pricing conditions?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Consignment variants require distinct document types (KB for Fill-up, KE for Issue, KA for Pickup, KR for Returns) and item categories (KBN, KEN, KAN, KRN) to enforce strict special stock handling and prevent incorrect billing behaviours. Reusing standard order types like OR would default to standard delivery-related billing and normal inventory movement types (like 601), bypassing customer consignment stock keys ('W'). Using standard SAP configuration tables (VOV7 for item categories and VOV8 for sales document types) ensures that movement types 631, 633, 634, and 653 are correctly assigned to the respective delivery types. This structural separation protects inventory integrity and auditing controls.
panel_qa.trap: We use standard orders for everything and just manually adjust the billing block if it is a consignment.

panel_qa.question: How does system performance and data volume scale when managing thousands of customer consignment stock locations in S/4HANA?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Managing extensive customer consignment stock requires utilizing table MSKU for special stock figures by customer, which can experience locking or performance degradation during massive concurrent goods movements if not indexed properly. We maintain performance by enforcing archive data strategies for historical consignment billing documents and utilizing standard S/4HANA simplification items for Material Ledger valuation. Furthermore, we leverage embedded EWM stock ledger optimizations to process goods issues and receipts asynchronously. This architectural approach guarantees sub-second response times for order entry and inventory availability checks.
panel_qa.trap: Database performance will naturally handle unlimited customer stock segments without needing any archiving or index tuning.

panel_qa.question: What audit controls prevent unauthorized or untracked physical movements between standard inventory and customer consignment inventory?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Audit controls are enforced by restricting movement types at the warehouse and inventory management levels, preventing ad-hoc transfers between unrestricted stock and special stock indicator 'W' without an underlying sales or transfer document. We configure authorization object M_MATE_STA and SD document approval workflows to mandate sales document references for all consignment pickups (KA) and returns (KR). Additionally, periodic cycle counting using transaction MI01 with special stock indicator 'W' ensures physical reconciliation with table MSKU balances. This completely eliminates shrinkage risk and ensures GAAP/IFRS compliance for consigned assets.
panel_qa.trap: Warehouse operators can freely move stock between standard and consignment bins whenever they feel like it.

panel_qa.question: How do we handle customer returns of unused consignment material versus defective consignment returns?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Unused consignment material returned by the customer is processed via Consignment Pickup (sales document type KA, item category KAN), which posts goods movement type 634, increasing customer consignment stock 'W' back into the designated storage location without generating a credit memo. Defective material or returns intended to be scrapped or restocked into company-owned inventory are processed via Consignment Returns (sales document type KR, item category KRN), posting goods movement 653 with special stock indicator 'W' and triggering a credit memo request. Copy control routines between delivery and billing are configured to allow credit generation only for KR, while KA remains non-billing relevant. This correctly bifurcates inventory restocking from financial crediting.
panel_qa.trap: We use the same return order type for both putting material back into customer consignment and issuing customer refunds.
